name: Water

sections.body: Vanilla RimWorld treats thirst as background texture. Sands of Arrakis makes it the first planning problem. Water is now a colony-wide logistics loop with consequences for labor, travel, heat management, clothing, and settlement layout.
sections.title: Overview

sections.body: Colonists spawn into a world where hydration is always running down. The meter begins high, but not safely high, which means a new settlement starts under pressure rather than comfort. That establishes the tone of Arrakis from the first morning.
sections.title: Water need

sections.body: Thirst is not constant. Hotter ambient bands and unroofed exposure accelerate loss, so the same stockpile of rations can feel generous indoors and suddenly inadequate once work shifts move onto open sand.
sections.title: Heat and exposure

sections.body: Stillsuits, reclamation masks, and headwraps are the player-facing answer to attrition. The system is intentionally generous enough to feel meaningful and intentionally capped so the player still respects water as a resource instead of solving it forever.
sections.title: Water retention

sections.body: The colony survives by turning atmosphere, time, and careful siting into sealed rations. Windtraps and portable condensers make water visible as infrastructure, while cisterns and hauling keep the network from collapsing under distance. A deep-vent plant can add a large sealed flow, but only on a rare steam geyser, and that building is a power jackpot first.
sections.title: Collectors and storage

sections.body: Reclaimed planting beds can grow sietch fiber as well as food and medicinals. A mature four-cell fiber harvest supplies 32 coarse fibers. Four native weaving bills at a sietch tailoring bench turn that into 24 Cloth, enough for the 20-Cloth construction pads of a passive sietch cooler; ongoing cooling consumes hauled water rather than burning Cloth. The complete growth cycle consumes two physical water rations and uses bed space that could grow food. Three configured growth days are not three guaranteed calendar days: light, temperature, irrigation and pawn labor determine the actual schedule. Wild Windcup supplies a smaller one-time fiber harvest and remains a sparse supplement.
sections.title: Water and local fabric

sections.body: Visiting caravans keep the water need. They arrive with conserved rations sized from the same heat and retention math colonists use, drink from that carried stock, and leave while still walking if the remaining reserve cannot cover the rest of the visit. They do not treat the sietch cistern as a free well.
sections.title: Traders and guests

sections.body: Research powered sietch cultivation. The trough retains native 2.8 fertility and 70 W pumps but accepts only reclaimed Arrakis crops. Its two-ration reserve starts empty and uses the same growth-accounted irrigation as reclaimed beds. More rapid growth consumes water faster without reducing the full-harvest charge. Power loss can kill crops through native trough behavior. Cultivation lights use 2,900 W while scheduled on; they switch off for plant rest. Heat, light, power, water and labor all remain relevant. The sietch ornamental planter grows only ornamental windcup, using existing plant art. Its one-ration reserve starts empty. Full establishment consumes half a ration; mature plants incur no ongoing water charge under the growth-based model. It yields no food, fiber or medicine and does not change wild windcup.
sections.title: Powered troughs and ornamental planters

sections.body: A deathstill reclaims two physical water rations once from an eligible fresh humanlike corpse and leaves marked remains. Burial and memorial caskets remain available. The 250 W sietch funerary chamber offers disposal of drained remains and a separate cleanup bill for rotten or otherwise ineligible organic bodies. Neither bill accepts fresh reclaimable human bodies or produces water. New bills require explicit permission for colonists and other non-hostiles. Strip equipment you want to keep before disposal. Thermal disposal is a practical game adaptation, not a canonical Fremen rite; old saved bills retain their chosen affiliation settings.

summary: Water is the central survival law of the mod. Heat, exposure, stillsuit discipline, storage, and collection all decide whether a colony merely works or actually endures.
